_comment: Root causes we have already established, keyed by the failing test case.
WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM annotations.json
An annotation is about one failure on one unit on one day. This is about a
test case: once the PCIe setup family was traced to the harness, every
future row of it starts from that answer instead of an empty cell. So this
file is small, hand-edited, reviewed, and committed — and the per-row
annotations still win over it, because a case with a known usual cause can
still fail for a different reason on a given unit.
rootCause is one of exactly two values, and that is the point:
setup - the test setup caused it. The DUT is not implicated.
dut   - a true DUT failure. The hardware is bad.
Anything more nuanced goes in `why`, which is prose and is displayed as the
note. A third value would immediately become a place to park uncertainty,
and 'unknown' is already what an unfilled row says.

PcieSetupTestCase.why: The PCIe setup case fails when the harness cannot enumerate the topology it expects — a proxy that has not come up, an inventory command that returned nothing parseable, or a topology file that does not match the server being tested. None of those are the module. Reported in Slack and the reason this case is treated as established.
PcieSetupTestCase.correctiveAction: Re-run once the RPC proxy is up and the expected topology matches the build. Escalate only if it reproduces on a second station.

CheckPcieTopology.why: The same failure as PcieSetupTestCase under the name our controllers actually record — the sheet calls it PcieSetupTestCase, the tracker logs CheckPcieTopology, and it is one thing. Discovered PCIe device count or parent/child topology not matching the expected server topology, which is a statement about the expectation as much as the hardware.
CheckPcieTopology.correctiveAction: Confirm the expected topology for this chassis build before touching the DUT. Re-run; escalate only on a second station.
